identity.title: LoRA-One: One-Step Full Gradient Could Suffice for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models, Provably and Efficiently

problem.claim: The paper studies how theory can guide practical large-language-model fine-tuning algorithms, using LoRA as a case study.

contributions.claim: The authors report a proof that, under gradient descent, LoRA adapters align with singular subspaces of the one-step full fine-tuning gradient.

They propose LoRA-One, which initializes adapters from the one-step full gradient and incorporates theoretically motivated preconditioners to address ill-conditioning; linear convergence and generalization are included in the theoretical framing.
The theory connects LoRA-One with other gradient-alignment methods and is used to clarify design misconceptions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a theory-driven LoRA algorithm based on immediate subspace alignment from the one-step full gradient, applicable to linear and nonlinear models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significant empirical improvements over LoRA and its variants across benchmarks covering natural language understanding, mathematical reasoning, and code generation.
The authors report that implementation code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames LoRA fine-tuning as a case study for theory-guided algorithm design.
It reports a gradient-descent proof linking LoRA adapter alignment to singular subspaces of the one-step full gradient.
This motivates immediate-gradient initialization, LoRA-One, preconditioning, and connections to related alignment methods.
The authors report improvements over LoRA and variants across language understanding, reasoning, and code benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The abstract couples a specific theoretical alignment result with an initialization rule and then names the algorithmic conditions it is intended to address, including ill-conditioning.

lessons.interpretation: A useful research pattern is to translate a structural theorem into a concrete initialization or optimization design choice, while retaining the theorem's scope and qualifications.
lessons.application: When proposing a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method, derive a measurable structural property and make it directly determine initialization or preconditioning, then state the applicable model and optimization assumptions.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when no reliable structural result links the proposed design choice to the target training behavior.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the assumptions, exact convergence/generalization statements, or which singular subspaces are selected.
It reports significant empirical improvements without giving datasets, metrics, baselines, numerical gains, or statistical conditions.
The abstract does not establish independent proof validity, reproducibility, or priority relative to prior work.
